PullRequest.Title: Allow Policy Helper registration through VS Code settings
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Let extensions register a Policy Helper for local Copilot Agent Host sessions without a VS Code restart or window reload.

The Agency extension can write `chat.agentHost.copilot.policyHelper` through the configuration API. VS Code forwards the registration to the local Agent Host. The Copilot runtime executes the helper and resolves policy.

Related issue: [github/copilot-agent-runtime#28101](https://github.com/github/copilot-agent-runtime/issues/28101).

## Extension contract

```ts
await vscode.workspace.getConfiguration('chat.agentHost.copilot').update(
    'policyHelper',
    { path: absoluteHelperPath, args: helperArguments },
    vscode.ConfigurationTarget.Global,
);
```

The setting accepts an executable `path` and optional string `args`. It uses application scope and excludes Settings Sync. The `advanced` tag limits default visibility in the Settings editor. `doNotSuggest: true` omits the key from settings JSON suggestions. The configuration API remains available, and users can inspect the value in raw settings JSON.

An unset, malformed, or whitespace-only path means no helper. Omitted arguments normalize to `[]`. A cleared setting crosses the protocol as an empty-path object, so removal clears the host's previous registration.

## Runtime lifecycle

The normalized registration belongs to the existing client startup snapshot. Addition, removal, path changes, and argument changes trigger the existing safe restart flow. Equivalent registrations do not trigger another restart.

Shared clients wait until active turns, subagents, and credential updates finish. Scoped clients refresh stale configuration at the next idle use. Each runtime launch receives the captured startup value. Change logs report `policyHelper` without its path or arguments.

The next fresh chat receives the helper configuration. Existing chats can retain their previous skill inventory after resume. Helper script content changes do not trigger a restart.

## Policy boundary

A valid registration sets `COPILOT_CLI_POLICY_HELPER` and adds `POLICY_HELPER` to `COPILOT_CLI_ENABLED_FEATURE_FLAGS`. Other feature flags remain intact. An absent registration clears the helper environment variable and adds no helper flag.

Device and server policy remain authoritative. VS Code provides registration, not policy enforcement. This change covers the local Agent Host path only. It does not change the Copilot extension's separate `copilotcli` session path.

## Validation

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `npx --yes --package=pnpm@12.16.0 pnpm run build-fast` | Passed, including client and built-in extensions |
| `npm run typecheck-client` | Passed |
| Targeted ESLint command below | Passed |
| `git diff --check` | Passed |
| Focused unit command below | 241 passed |

```powershell
npm run eslint -- src\vs\platform\agentHost\common\copilotCliConfig.ts src\vs\platform\agentHost\node\copilot\copilotAgent.ts src\vs\platform\agentHost\node\copilot\copilotAgentStartupConfig.ts src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\common\copilotCliConfig.test.ts src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\copilotAgent.test.ts src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\copilotAgentStartupConfig.test.ts src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\browser\chat.shared.contribution.ts src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\chatConfiguration.test.ts

.\scripts\test.bat --reporter dot --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\common\copilotCliConfig.test.ts --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\copilotAgentStartupConfig.test.ts --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\copilotAgent.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\chatConfiguration.test.ts --grep "copilotCliConfig|CopilotAgentStartupConfig|Chat configuration|CopilotAgent (restart on startup config change|scoped credentials)"
```

The tests cover normalization, registration metadata, removal transport, environment injection, redacted comparisons, captured startup values, scoped clients, and deferred restarts.

## Live verification

An isolated regular Code OSS workbench used a cloned profile and a Windows ARM64 runtime override. The source profile remained untouched.

| Scenario | Observed result |
|---|---|
| Register through an extension with `ConfigurationTarget.Global` | Client restarted automatically without an application relaunch |
| Invoke the generated skill in the next fresh chat | Actual skill invocation returned `policy helper skill for repo devprod.commitlinks` |
| Clear the registration | Client restarted automatically, and a fresh chat reported the skill unavailable |
| Change arguments during an active turn | The skill call completed successfully before the deferred restart |
| Write an identical registration again | No additional restart |
| Resume a chat that started without the helper | The previous skill inventory remained |

The live run used runtime artifact `70ffdab`, not the bundled runtime. It does not establish published runtime availability. Full integration and smoke suites, remote hosts, and the Agency rollout gate were not exercised.

## Manual test

1. Configure a compatible runtime and a helper that supplies a repository-specific skill.
2. Start a local Agent Host chat.
3. Write the helper registration through the extension configuration API.
4. Open a fresh chat without a window reload.
5. Invoke the generated skill.
6. During an active turn, change the helper arguments.
7. Confirm that the turn finishes before the client restart.
8. Clear the registration and open a fresh chat.
9. Confirm that the helper skill is absent.

Scenarios.Scenario: Launch a local Copilot Agent Host client with a configured policy helper
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Renderer configuration is mirrored to the local Agent Host, then client acquisition snapshots the normalized helper, serializes it into the subprocess environment, loads certificates/runtime paths, and starts the Copilot runtime before chat work can proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch the full mirrored root-configuration patch to the Agent Host on connect or reconnect.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One root-config action per client connect/reconnect; the policy-helper value is one field in the existing grouped patch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The grouped configuration IPC already occurred, but it did not include a policy-helper field.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: On initial connection it supplies startup state before the runtime is acquired; reconnect dispatch is asynchronous protocol work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start the Copilot runtime with COPILOT_CLI_POLICY_HELPER and the POLICY_HELPER feature flag.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One runtime start for the shared client; scoped credential clients each retain their existing one-client-per-chat ownership.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same runtime subprocess was started; this diff only adds one environment value and feature flag when explicitly configured.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runtime startup is on first chat/client acquisition's critical path; the added environment manipulation is constant-size for normal helper arguments.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: Copilot runtime policy-helper integration configured by src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgent.ts:4341
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: The external policy helper may be executed by the runtime when policy is resolved.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Runtime-defined and not established by repository code; enabled only when the user/extension explicitly configures a helper.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: VS Code did not opt the runtime into the configured external policy helper.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Potentially part of runtime policy resolution, but invocation frequency and scheduling are outside the reviewed diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Normally one helper registration with a short path and argument list; subprocess cardinality follows existing shared/scoped client ownership, not the argument count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Shared client startup is coalesced by _clientStarting/_ensureClientHealing. Scoped clients remain isolated per credential-bearing chat and can start independently, as before.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Startup configuration is snapshotted per client; equivalent normalized registrations compare equal and reuse the running client. Runtime paths/certificates follow existing startup caches and reads.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the IPC and runtime startup call path; insufficient evidence that the small added serialization/environment work causes measurable degradation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The runtime's helper invocation cost and frequency are unavailable in this repository, so no regression can be inferred from enabling the explicitly requested integration.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The expensive runtime boundary already exists on client acquisition, and execution of the configured helper is opt-in required behavior whose frequency is not proven here.

Scenarios.Scenario: Add, change, or remove the policy-helper registration while shared chats are active or idle
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A configuration change crosses one IPC root-config action, startup snapshots are compared, and an effective change requests one shared-client restart. Busy turns, subagents, and credential updates finish first; the next client use pays runtime startup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the transformed helper registration or empty-path removal object to the local Agent Host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One action per effective application-setting change; unrelated configuration events are filtered by affectsConfiguration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Policy-helper setting changes had no mirrored action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Triggers host-side comparison; it does not block an already active turn.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stop the shared Copilot client and start a replacement lazily after configuration changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one shared restart for coalesced pending reasons once all live work is idle; repeated equivalent normalized values cause zero restarts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Policy-helper changes did not restart the runtime; other startup-baked settings already used this restart flow.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Deferred off active turns, but the next operation requiring the client pays replacement startup latency.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Schedule model-catalog refresh after stopping the old runtime.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One scheduled refresh per applied shared-client restart, using the existing refresh coalescing path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No restart/model refresh occurred for policy-helper setting changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the stop path via a fire-and-forget schedule; last-known models remain published while it runs.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reload certificates, resolve runtime paths, and potentially write the user-data certificate file during replacement startup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per replacement client startup under the existing startup logic.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These operations already accompanied every runtime restart; the diff adds policy-helper changes as a deliberate restart trigger.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Part of replacement startup paid on next client acquisition.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost is constant per batch of effective helper changes before the idle boundary, independent of chat count for the shared client.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Pending shared restart reasons are stored in a Set and drained once. Active turns/subagents and credential updates gate teardown, preventing overlapping shared restarts.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The normalized path/args are serialized deterministically; omitted args become [], so semantically equivalent objects hit the equality check. Removal normalizes to undefined after transport.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that an effective change causes one deferred shared-runtime restart and equivalent writes do not.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Runtime startup duration varies by certificates, runtime path resolution, and environment, but the restart is required to change startup-only environment and is bounded/coalesced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The expensive work is bounded, coalesced, deferred away from active work, and necessary to apply a startup-only value.

Scenarios.Scenario: Use credential-scoped chats after a policy-helper change
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each scoped chat checks its client's captured startup snapshot at its next idle credential boundary. A stale scoped client/session is stopped and replaced before that chat sends through the updated runtime.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stop and replace a stale credential-scoped Copilot runtime, then resume/recreate the chat session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one replacement for each scoped chat actually used after the change; effective cardinality is the number of distinct credential-scoped chats subsequently activated.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A helper change did not stale scoped snapshots; existing startup-config changes already used the same lazy replacement mechanism.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Replacement is on that chat's next-send critical path, but never interrupts an active turn or subagent.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Perform existing certificate and runtime-path startup work for each replacement scoped client.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per activated stale scoped client.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The work already occurred whenever a scoped client was created or replaced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks each affected chat's replacement startup.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of distinct credential-scoped chats used after the effective setting change, not total stored chats or messages.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each chat owns a scoped client; replacements are serialized by that chat's boundary but independent chats can replace concurrently. No new global limiter is added, though the setting is expected to change rarely and inactive chats do no work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each scoped client stores its startup snapshot; once replaced it is warm for subsequent sends until another effective startup configuration change. Equivalent helper values do not mark it stale.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in lazy per-scoped-client replacement; low confidence that realistic usage produces a harmful burst rather than a small, required set of replacements.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The repository does not establish a realistically large number of concurrently active credential-scoped chats or frequent helper changes; the observed mechanism is bounded to used chats.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Multiplicity follows existing security isolation, inactive clients are not eagerly restarted, and evidence does not establish a realistic harmful concurrency burst.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all eight changed files and traced configuration mirroring, normalization/serialization, shared restart coalescing, scoped-client refresh, runtime startup, filesystem/certificate work, model-refresh networking, and the opt-in helper subprocess boundary. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
